family.tagline: A stationery shop below, a reporter's desk above, one Companion Core.
family.story: Nasrin runs the stationery shop on the ground floor of their building. Saeed reports for a living from the Desk Nook upstairs, where the Companion Core sits on his desk. One Core serves them both.

home.lede: A pale-rendered mid-rise stands on a city street, with shops behind tall glass below and a teal lobby door. The flat on the first floor up opens its living room and kitchen onto a steel-railed balcony over the street.

spots.line: A writing desk, a laptop and a ladder shelf, with the Core on the desk.
A sofa, a club chair and a trunk coffee table on a wide rug.
An L of counters with a range, a fridge and a window over the sink.
A bistro table and two bentwood chairs above the shopfronts.
A washing machine and a dryer side by side in a narrow closet.

day.line: Saeed reads the morning's feeds at the counter with his coffee.
Nasrin draws in the morning light at the balcony table.
Nasrin writes up the school's order on the sofa after lunch.
Saeed rides to an interview from the street door.
Saeed's hours for each piece add up.
Nasrin checks how many people looked at the new range.
Saeed goes through the week's renewals at the counter.
The shop's regulars gather for the lettering evening.

members.name: Nasrin
members.work: runs a stationery shop in the building

companion.name: Sumac
companion.job: Opens Invoice Ninja in its own browser and drafts the invoices Nasrin lists.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Nasrin reads every line before it stands.

profile.bio: Nasrin runs the stationery shop below the flat and does the shop's books on the sofa. Her invoices, stock and customer list sit on the Core, and Sumac drafts the invoices she approves.

companion.name: Barberry
companion.job: Lists the claims in Saeed's notes that have no source beside them.
companion.limits: Lists only. Saeed checks every claim against the file.

profile.bio: Saeed reports from the Desk Nook, where the Core sits on his desk. His notes, saved pages and records are plain files there, and Barberry lists the claims he still has to check.

popup.title: The courier stops at the shop
popup.body: The courier leaves the Core with Nasrin at the shop door. Saeed carries the package up the stairs to the flat.

popup.title: What is inside the package
popup.body: Saeed cuts the tape on the writing desk. Inside are the Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive.

popup.title: Plugged in on the desk
popup.body: Saeed plugs the Core in by the desk lamp, and Nasrin presses the button. It wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Nasrin joins from her phone
popup.body: Nasrin joins the Core's own network from her phone's Wi-Fi settings. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Hermes for Saeed, OpenClaw for Nasrin
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Saeed picks Hermes and Nasrin picks OpenClaw. The couple adds Obsidian and Invoice Ninja, then walks away.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

detail.after: Duplicati copies the chosen folders to a local disk on the shelf, with encryption, as they leave the Core.

Choose the disk on the shelf
Set the Friday schedule

popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

detail.after: ArchiveBox saves a searchable, dated copy of each page he cites on the Core. The copy opens when the live page no longer does.

Open the copy if the page changes

Read the hours per client on Friday

popup.title: One Core above the shopfronts
popup.body: Invoices, event lists, reporting notes and morning feeds run on one Companion Core, in a flat above the shops.

closing.body: Your invoices, orders and reporting notes can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Paperless-ngx is over the 40 percent app cap, so the plan's paperless was swapped. Papra is told in two other flats and is left out here; the plan lists Twenty instead.
Whisper-WebUI would suit Saeed's interview tape but has no QA screenshot, so it needs an owner entry in reviewed.json; it is left out and the tape is not told.
Umami and Hi.Events carry the catalog's public-access caveat. Each beat carries the note and tells a count or a guest list at home, never a public link.
Listmonk sending needs an outside mail provider; the beat says so and promises no delivery. Docuseal: the supplier signs in the room, never from outside the home network.
Endurain: syncing out is optional (catalog caveat); the beat logs rides only and makes no health claim. Wallos carries its logo-fetch note.
Barberry (Hermes) acts on Obsidian through its MCP entry and only lists; Sumac (OpenClaw) opens Invoice Ninja and only drafts. Both are approved line by line by their owner.

Camera: the first run walks the street to the Core, then every room beat is on the second level; the only walk off it is down to the street for out-front and the outro. No TV: the couch media beat is the podcast.
No third-party app is in more than two of the six apartments: Vikunja, Kimai, Activepieces, draw.io and CryptPad are this flat's. Kimai and the Homarr start page are pair-less.
